A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Rollout Roulette research and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, appendices A–H, and checklist. Reflow and relocated content can be matched reliably; pages 9–27 are textually and visually identical.

before.justification: v4 reports original benchmark evaluations, reward-model and temperature ablations, and appendix experiments on particle Gibbs and parallel compute allocation (Tables 1–3; Figures 4–7).

after.justification: v5 retains these original benchmark results, ablations, and appendix experiments unchanged.

M1.justification: The particle-filtering procedure, reward aggregation, final-answer selection, and particle Gibbs/parallel-tempering extensions remain unchanged in Section 3 and the appendices.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same mathematical, financial, and chemistry reasoning coverage: MATH500, AIME 2024, FinanceBench, and NumGLUE Task 2.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same comparator membership, including Greedy, Self Consistency, BoN/WBoN, Beam Search, and DVTS where originally included. The Section 5 TSMC comparison is also unchanged.

E3.justification: The 32-generation main comparison, 64-generation appendix comparison, temperature settings, ablation subsets, and Appendix H parsing and scoring procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: The PRM-choice, reward-aggregation, and temperature ablations in Figure 5 and the particle Gibbs/parallel-allocation analyses in Appendix B and Figures 6–7 are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain the same reporting practices and checklist acknowledgment that systematic error bars are unavailable. The statement about repeated development experiments remains unquantified; no run counts, seeds, or statistical procedures are added.

E6.justification: All result entries and plotted results match. For example, Table 1 retains Qwen2.5-Math-7B particle filtering at 87.7 on MATH500 and 10/30 on AIME; relocated Table 2 retains 70.33 on FinanceBench and 84.22 on NumGLUE.

T1.justification: The state-space definitions, posterior equations, expected-accuracy theorem, Appendix C proof, and parallel-tempering acceptance formula are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions and performance claims, including the 4–16x scaling advantage and the small-model claims at four and 32 rollouts.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning early pruning, reward uncertainty, and generalization beyond mathematics are unchanged. The limitations concerning reward-model latency, prompt formatting, and domain-dependent budget tuning are also retained.

D1.justification: v5 adds an abstract link advertised as providing code and further information, absent from v4. Other technical details are unchanged. The retained checklist still promises code release upon acceptance, so the PDFs establish a new access pointer but leave actual availability unresolved.

R1.justification: Section 5 and the reference list are identical, including the positioning against Twisted SMC. No cited works or relationships to prior research change.

P1.justification: The abstract gains one short code-access sentence, and the arXiv version/date label changes. The scientific prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged after matching page-break differences.

P2.justification: The abstract and opening pages reflow. Table 2 moves from page 7 beside Section 4.3 to page 8 beside Section 4.4, changing surrounding text wrapping. Its contents and the figure graphics remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new abstract link modestly improves resource discoverability by giving readers a specific project/code pointer that v4 lacked. Scientific support is unchanged. The benefit is limited by conflicting retained checklist wording about future code release and the less convenient placement of Table 2 away from its discussion.
